body:
## Summary
Move the per-stage aging cadence off per-browser localStorage and onto the workspace's board axis (an optional `slaDays` on each stage in the `pipelineStages` decision-config phase), written through one narrow, lock-safe `PATCH /api/pipeline/stage-sla`. Every surface that asks "is this candidate aging?" - the board chip, the sidebar badge, and the policy pass r02 already approved - then reads the same team-owned number through `slaForStage(stage, _, axis)`.

## Description
Today the SLA editor says in its own copy that cadences are "Saved for this browser". Two recruiters on the same team therefore age the same board differently, and the shared counter (`attentionCounts`, which feeds the sidebar badge, the palette preview and the companion digest) silently uses role defaults - so the badge and the board's Aging chip disagree the moment anyone tunes a column, with nothing saying which is right. The registry's technique for exactly this seam (`overridable-defaults-with-a-server-side-approximation`) has an explicit exit: *if overrides can live in the store the shared computation reads, use them and skip the approximation*. Here they can: the axis is already per-workspace, org/team tiered, validated, and read by every server consumer that resolves stages by role.

The move: `StageDef.slaDays?` (validated integer 1..365, refused on the terminal role), carried by `toStageDef` and the composer's `draftToStored`; `slaForStage` gains the axis layer (explicit override -> axis `slaDays` -> role default -> legacy fallback), so `attention.ts` inherits the team value without an edit. The board's editor writes through a new `PATCH /api/pipeline/stage-sla` that uses `updateDecisionConfig(..., 'team')` (IMMEDIATE, re-reads the current axis) and requires `pipeline:write` like every other axis write. `usePipelineSla` stops reading localStorage; it offers any leftover local cadences once as an explicit "apply to the team" action (never a silent import of one browser's taste into team policy) and clears them after a successful write.

## Flow
1. Schema: add `slaDays` to `PipelineStageWire` / `STAGE_KEYS`, validate in `validateStage`, thread through `toStageDef` and `pipelineAxisDraft.wire()`.
2. `slaForStage`: consult `axis.find(id).slaDays` between the override and the role default.
3. Route: `PATCH /api/pipeline/stage-sla {stage, days|null}` -> `requireOperator` + `pipeline:write` -> `updateDecisionConfig('pipelineStages', setStageSla, ws, 'team')`; refusals answer `DECISION_CONFIG_INVALID` (existing code); `npm run api:docs` regenerates the reference row.
4. Client: `usePipelineSla` derives values from the board axis, keeps an optimistic in-memory override until the next load, exposes `pendingLocalAdoption`; the editor shows the team value, a save-failed line via `useErrorMessage`, and the new copy "Applies to everyone on this team" in 4 locales.
5. Doc: pipeline README's SLA section and Known gaps.

## Expected impact
One answer to "is this candidate aging" per team instead of one per browser; the sidebar badge stops contradicting the board for every tuned workspace; the approved r02 aging-clock card gets a server-readable SLA to follow instead of inventing a second policy table; a new recruiter's first visit sees the team's cadences instead of role defaults. Removes a per-browser tenancy workaround (the SLA half of `pipelineBoardStorage` + its legacy-key migration).

## Evaluation
Claim: the aging cadence becomes team data that the board, the attention badge and a server writer all resolve identically, and no axis writer can erase it.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass.
After: 7 of 7.
Method: gate - node:test cases in app/_lib/stage-sla.test.ts (schema, axis round-trip, slaForStage, attentionCounts over a temp KP_DB_PATH, adoption helper) and app/api/pipeline/stage-sla/route.test.ts (write, scope, refusals, capability), then the challenge integrationGate (tsc, lint, i18n:check, api:check, docs:check, test:unit).
Result: pending - measured by the builder.
Gate: contract

body:
## Summary
The map board replaced the card board but left its two working modes behind: in select mode a recruiter cannot pick a single bead (only 'select all shown'), and no bead can be moved from the board at all. Port both onto the Subway as one operation with two inputs - select mode turns beads and stations into checkboxes, and outside it a bead can be dragged to a legal station on its own line or moved from a keyboard/right-click 'Move to' menu, both through one pure legality module and the board's existing optimistic, CAS-guarded moveEntry.

## Description
The bulk bar (move, accept/reject, invite, outreach) is the board's strongest verb, and on the shipped board it only works on whatever the filters leave visible: `toggleSelected` exists and nothing calls it, and a bead click still opens the modal while the bar says 'Select'. Moving one candidate takes three steps (bead -> modal -> footer select) although `usePipelineBoardData.moveEntry` already does optimistic paint, rollback, the bounced-bead reason and an events-only reconcile - reachable today only from the off-axis strip. This card makes the Subway act on what the recruiter points at: a bead in select mode is a `role=checkbox` with a selected ring; a station in select mode toggles its whole cell (partial -> all, all -> none) instead of opening the Orchard; the '+N' roster items toggle too. Outside select mode a bead is draggable onto stations of its own line that `moveTargetStages` allows (the terminal stage and its own column refuse visibly), and Shift+F10 / right-click opens the existing `PipelineCandidateMenu` with the same targets - both calling one `dropMove` so the keyboard path cannot decay (registry: drag-drop / keyboard-alternatives). Cell selection goes through a new `setSelectedMany` in usePipelineBulk that dispatches `selectionChanged`, so an armed bulk reject/outreach confirm disarms exactly as a single toggle does.

## Flow
1. `map/subway/subwayInteraction.ts` (pure): `beadIntent`, `beadA11y`, `cellSelectState`, `toggleCellSelection`, `canDropOn`, `dropMove`, `moveMenuItems` - tests first.
2. usePipelineBulk: `setSelectedMany(ids, on)` (clears bulkResult, dispatches selectionChanged); usePipelineTabState + PipelinePopulatedBoard pass it and `axis` through.
3. PipelineBoardSubway / LineRow / Bead: read selectMode + selectedIds; station button toggles the cell in select mode; bead is checkbox in select mode, draggable + menu door otherwise (drag source on a wrapper span - Firefox does not start a drag from a button); legal stations highlight while a drag is live, illegal ones refuse.
4. Catalogs: cell-select aria ('Select all {count} in {stage}'), drop-target hint - 4 locales; reuse candidateRow.selectCandidate / moveTo.
5. README: close the first Known gaps bullet, describe the two modes.

## Expected impact
The board's batch verbs work on a hand-picked cohort for the first time since the redesign; a single stage move drops from three steps and a modal to one gesture or one menu; the dormant move machine and the orphaned card-row grammar become the shipped behaviour again. Closes three open leftover items in one coherent build.

## Evaluation
Claim: select mode can build any cohort from beads and stations, and a bead moves from the board by drag or keyboard through one legality rule and the existing CAS move.
Before: 0 of 6 acceptance cases pass.
After: 6 of 6.
Method: gate - node:test cases in app/features/hiring/pipeline/map/subway/subwayInteraction.test.ts, then the challenge integrationGate (tsc, lint, i18n:check, design:check, test:unit); a both-theme visual check of the selected ring and drop highlight.
Result: pending - measured by the builder.
Gate: none
